name: Hooks

hero.title: 65 hooks. Zero cleanup code to write.
hero.lede: From `useToggle` and `useClickOutside` to `useShare`, `useBiometrics` and `useGeolocation`. Each one removes its own listeners, timers and observers when the component unmounts, renders safely on the server, and hands back signals you can read anywhere.

facts.value: 65 in one package<small>State, DOM, responsive, timing, device, data, composition.</small>
automatic on unmount<small>Listeners, observers and timers are removed for you.</small>
SSR-safe<small>Browser APIs are guarded; nothing throws during server rendering.</small>
{dot:warn}45 of 65 compile to iOS and Android<small>Counted on main. Native targets are experimental.</small>

why.title: The helpers you keep copying from blog posts, done properly once.

items.title: Nothing to clean up
items.text: Every listener, observer, interval and timeout is registered against the component and removed on unmount. There is no `return () => removeEventListener(…)` to forget.

items.title: Signals in, signals out
items.text: Stateful hooks return accessors such as `online()` or `visibility()`. Pass one to another hook as a getter and it reacts, so `useInterval(fn, () => visible() ? 30_000 : null)` pauses itself when the tab hides.

items.title: The edge cases are already handled
items.text: `useScrollLock` is reference-counted and pads for the scrollbar so the page does not jump. `useClickOutside` listens to `pointerdown`, so one tap fires once. `useClipboard` ignores a slower, older copy that resolves last.

items.title: One call, three platforms
items.text: `useShare`, `useHaptics`, `useBiometrics`, `useImagePicker` and 41 others compile to native code for iOS and Android. Three are web-only by design (`useBreakpoint`, a width `useMediaQuery`, `useControllableState`): a native build drops them with a named warning instead of guessing.

difference.title: Pause polling while nobody is looking.

before.label: React · hand-rolled
before.caption: A visibility hook, a ref so the interval sees the latest callback, and two dependency arrays to keep right.

after.label: Pyreon · @pyreon/hooks
after.caption: The delay is a getter. When the tab hides it returns null and the interval stops; when it comes back, it restarts. Unmount clears it.

items.name: DOM:
items.text: click outside, hover, focus, element size, intersection, infinite scroll, scroll lock

items.name: Focus for overlays:
items.text: useFocusTrap stacks nested modals; useInertOthers makes the background inert and restores it exactly

items.name: Timing:
items.text: debounced values and callbacks, throttling, intervals with a reactive delay, a self-updating useTimeAgo

items.name: Device:
items.text: clipboard, haptics, share sheet, notifications, biometrics, camera, image and file pickers, speech, wake lock

items.name: Data:
items.text: useFetch aborts the previous request on refetch and on unmount, so a slow response never overwrites a fresh one

items.name: Cross-platform state:
items.text: useAuth, useDatabase, useMap, usePush, usePayments mirror their native containers field for field

items.name: Secrets stay off disk:
items.text: useSecureStorage uses the Keychain on iOS, AndroidKeyStore on Android, and memory only on the web

items.name: Newly native:
items.text: useDocumentVisibility, usePrevious, useUpdateEffect, useReducedMotion, useKeyboard, useLatest and `prefers-color-scheme` queries now compile for iOS and Android

limits.title: Device hooks ask for permission
limits.text: Camera, notifications, location and the microphone prompt the user and can be refused. `useAudioRecorder().start()` and `useDeviceMotion().start()` resolve `false` on a refusal, so a denial is an `if`, not a `try`.

limits.title: Web APIs vary by browser
limits.text: Web Bluetooth, the Share API and wake lock are not in every browser. Check the hook's own flag first: `canShare()` on `useShare`, `available()` on `useBluetooth`, `supported()` on `useWakeLock`.

limits.title: Native lowering is experimental
limits.text: Hooks that compile to iOS and Android follow the native compiler's status. Some take a narrower shape natively (a literal key for `useKeyboard`, a string URL for `useFetch`); anything else is a named warning.

comingFrom.title: useClickAway → useClickOutside
comingFrom.note: The element is passed as a getter, so it can mount and unmount while the listener stays in place.

comingFrom.title: useMediaQuery returns an accessor
comingFrom.note: In React the whole component re-renders when the query flips. Here only the text node that reads `wide()` updates.

recipes.title: A dialog that behaves
recipes.text: Focus moves in and stays in, the page behind stops scrolling, Escape and a click outside both close it. Four hooks, no cleanup code.
recipes.code:
import { effect, signal } from '@pyreon/reactivity' import { useClickOutside, useFocusTrap, useKeyboard, useScrollLock } from '@pyreon/hooks' export function Dialog(props: { open: () => boolean; onClose: () => void }) { const panel = signal(null) const scroll = useScrollLock() useFocusTrap(() => panel(), { active: () => props.open(), initialFocus: true }) useClickOutside(() => panel(), () => props.onClose()) useKeyboard('Escape', () => props.onClose()) effect(() => (props.open() ? scroll.lock() : scroll.unlock())) return () => props.open() ? (
panel.set(el)} role="dialog" aria-modal="true">
) : null }

faq.q: Do I still write dependency arrays?
faq.a: No. A hook reads signals, so it knows what it depends on. `useUpdateEffect(source, callback)` takes a getter, which is the opposite order from React's `(effect, deps)`.

Browser APIs are guarded, so a hook renders its server value (for example `useOnline()` is `true`, `useDocumentVisibility()` is `"visible"`). `useFetch` starts pending on the server too, so the hydrated page matches the server HTML.

faq.q: Which hooks work on iOS and Android?
faq.a: 45 of the 65 compile to native code. The DOM-only ones (focus traps, element size, scroll lock and similar) stay on the web, and three are web-only by design with a named compile warning: `useBreakpoint`, a width or orientation `useMediaQuery`, and `useControllableState`. Use `useSizeClass()` for compact versus regular layouts on every platform.

faq.q: Does importing one hook pull in all 65?
faq.a: No. The package is ESM and marked side-effect free, so a bundler keeps only the hooks you import.

faq.q: Is `useFetch` a replacement for a data library?
faq.a: It is deliberately thin: one request, abort on refetch and unmount, no cache, no retries. For caching and signal-driven keys use `@pyreon/query`.
